stories.name: Intel Turnaround Rally
stories.blurb: Intel's stock and analyst sentiment have been rallying on optimism that its turnaround strategy and AI-driven demand are gaining traction ahead of and following Q2 earnings.

stories.name: Intel and Musk's Terafab
stories.blurb: Intel remains a key partner in Elon Musk's Terafab AI chip venture as Musk clarifies that TSMC may only sublease space and will not operate the fab.

stories.name: AI Chip Selloff
stories.blurb: A broad global selloff in AI and semiconductor stocks, driven by fading enthusiasm for AI trade and weak guidance, has pushed the Nasdaq into correction.

stories.name: AMD Stock Surge
stories.blurb: AMD's stock has crossed $1 trillion amid growing AI optimism, a Microsoft partnership, and debate over whether it remains a good buy.

stories.name: Intel SK Hynix talks
stories.blurb: Intel and SK Hynix are reportedly in talks for a deal to manufacture memory chips in the U.S., sending both companies' shares higher.

stories.name: AI chip stock rally
stories.blurb: Investors are debating whether the surging valuations of AI chipmakers like NVIDIA and Marvell are justified by future growth or due for a pullback.

stories.name: ASML AI chip demand
stories.blurb: ASML is ramping up EUV lithography production and attracting investor attention as surging AI chip demand drives competition among major semiconductor players.

stories.name: AI Chip Market Growth
stories.blurb: A collection of market reports highlighting how AI, 5G, and edge computing are driving rapid growth across semiconductors, chipsets, and related hardware markets where Intel competes.

past.name: Intel-SK Hynix Ohio Deal
past.blurb: Intel is reportedly in talks with SK Hynix to manufacture memory chips at Intel's underused Ohio fab, boosting Intel's stock alongside a separate $15 billion capital raise for AI chip growth.

past.name: AI chip selloff
past.blurb: A broad selloff in AI-related chip and memory stocks, driven by bubble fears and weak guidance, is dragging down markets worldwide.

past.name: Meta Muse AI Chip Rally
past.blurb: Meta's new Muse AI agent sparked expectations of increased CPU demand, sending Intel, AMD, and Arm shares sharply higher amid broader moves in the AI chip sector.

past.name: Apple Ditching Qualcomm
past.blurb: Apple is gradually replacing Qualcomm's modem chips with its own in-house designs, raising questions about Qualcomm's future revenue and stock performance.

7.text: Intel reports Q3 earnings October 29, with analysts expecting $0.39 EPS (up 69.6% YoY) and $16.44B revenue (up 20.4% YoY). Coverage cites rising margins, server CPU demand and pricing strength, foundry progress, and volatile post-earnings swings.

16.text: October 26: Musk claims the Texas chip fab Tesla and SpaceX are building will rank in the top 20 of country GDP from a single building and is courting about 10 Korean suppliers. Intel is not mentioned.

5.text: Chip stocks fell sharply on AI-spending and supply-chain warnings from Lam Research and SK Hynix, with Intel dropping 7% and peers like AMD and Marvell sinking 8%. A brief rebound followed Super Micro's strong guidance and an Elon Musk comment, but investors now await Intel's earnings next week.

11.text: AMD landed hyperscaler AI deals and posted 50% revenue growth, yet its stock fell sharply and trades at a very high multiple ahead of November 3 earnings. One article argues Arm, not Intel or AMD, is the better CPU play for agentic AI.

15.text: Intel is progressing on Arizona and Ohio fabs, with Arizona equipment installation underway and Ohio targeting 2030–2031 production. Intel is also partnering with Tesla and SpaceX on Musk's Terafab AI chip project, a $16.8 billion effort.

12.text: STMicroelectronics, ASE Technology, Cadence, and ASML all reported AI-driven demand: rising revenues, record packaging sales, strong backlogs, and lithography orders extending to 2030. Intel isn't mentioned; the articles bear on it only as evidence of broad AI chip demand.

13.text: Intel is named as a player in reports on photonic ICs, IPMI, ASIC design services, and flip chip packaging, but the articles give no Intel-specific figures or announcements. The remaining items—rugged laptops, AV2 codec adoption, Sickbay, and SUNMI—barely involve Intel.
